cues.zh: 我把这些数据交给了学生。这些数据来自一则蓝十字蓝盾的广告，这则广告刊登在《新闻周刊》杂志上。

cues.en: and the ad gave these figures to show the cost escalation of gallbladder surgery
cues.zh: 广告给出了这些数字，用来展示胆囊手术成本的不断攀升，

cues.en: in the years since 1950 when that surgery cost $361
cues.zh: 自 1950 年该手术费用为 361 美元以来的这些年里。

cues.en: I said make a semi logarithmic plot, let's see what's happening.
cues.zh: 我说，画一个半对数图，让我们看看发生了什么。

cues.en: The students found that the first four points lined up on a straight line whose slope indicated inflation of about 6%
cues.zh: 学生们发现前四个点排在一条直线上，其斜率表明通货膨胀率约为每年

cues.en: per year. But the fourth, fifth and sixth were on a steeper line, almost 10%
cues.zh: 6%。但第四、第五和第六个点在一条更陡峭的直线上，通货膨胀率接近每年

cues.en: inflation per year.
Well, then I said to the students, Run that steeper line on out to the year 2000.
cues.zh: 然后我对学生们说，把那条更陡峭的线延伸到 2000 年。

cues.en: Let's get an idea what gallbladder surgery might cost.
cues.zh: 让我们大致了解一下胆囊手术到时候可能要花多少钱。

cues.en: The answer is $25,000
cues.zh: 答案是 25,000 美元。

cues.en: The lesson there is awfully clear.
cues.zh: 其中的教训非常明显。

cues.en: If you're thinking about gallbladder surgery, do it now.
cues.zh: 如果你在考虑做胆囊手术，现在就做吧。

cues.en: In
cues.zh: 在

cues.en: the summer of nineteen eighty six,
cues.zh: 1986 年的夏天，

cues.en: the news reports indicated that the world population
cues.zh: 新闻报道显示世界人口

cues.en: had reached the number 5,000,000,000
people growing at the rate of one point seven percent per year. Well, reaction to one point seven might be to say, That's so small!
cues.zh: 人，正以每年 1.7% 的速度增长。嗯，对 1.7% 的反应可能会是：这太少了吧！

cues.en: Nothing bad could ever happen at 1.7%
cues.zh: 每年 1.7% 的增长率

cues.en: per year. So you calculate the doubling time, you find it's only forty one years.
cues.zh: 绝不会引发任何坏事。所以你算一下翻倍时间，会发现只有四1年。

cues.en: More recently,
cues.zh: 更近一些的

cues.en: we read that the world population had increased from 5,000,000,000 to 6,000,000,000 people.
cues.zh: 我们读到世界人口从 50 亿增加到了 60 亿。

cues.en: The good news is that the growth rate had dropped from 1.7%
cues.zh: 好消息是增长率已经从每年

cues.en: per year to 1.3%
cues.zh: 1.7% 下降到了

cues.en: per year. The bad news is that in spite of the drop in the growth rate, the world population today is increasing by something over 80,000,000
cues.zh: 1.3%。坏消息是，尽管增长率下降了，如今的世界人口每年仍在增加

cues.en: people
every year.
cues.zh: 人。

cues.en: Now if this modest current 1.3
cues.zh: 如果目前这温和的每年 1.3%

cues.en: per year could continue, the world population would grow to a density of one person per square meter on the dry land surface of the earth in just seven and eighty years and the mass of people would equal the mass of the earth in just two thousand four hundred years.
cues.zh: 的增长率持续下去，只需 780 年，地球陆地表面的世界人口密度就会达到每平方米一个人，而且只需 2400 年，人口的总质量就会等于地球的质量。

cues.en: Now we can smile at those. We know they couldn't happen.
cues.zh: 现在我们可以对这些数字付诸一笑。我们知道这绝不可能发生。

cues.en: This one makes for a cute cartoon. The caption says, Excuse me, sir, but I am prepared to make you a rather attractive offer for your square.
cues.zh: 这个很适合做成一幅可爱的漫画。说明文字写着：打扰一下，先生，我准备为你的这方土地向你提出一个相当诱人的报价。

cues.en: Now there's a very profound lesson in that cartoon. The lesson is that zero population growth is going to happen.
cues.zh: 这幅漫画里包含着一个非常深刻的教训。这个教训就是，人口零增长势在必行。

cues.en: Now we can debate whether we like zero population growth or don't like it.
cues.zh: 现在我们可以争论我们是喜欢还是不喜欢人口零增长。

cues.en: It's going to happen whether we debate it or not, whether we like it or not. It's absolutely certain people could not live at that density on the dry land surface of the earth. Therefore, today's high birth rates will drop,
cues.zh: 无论我们争论与否，无论我们喜欢与否，它都会发生。人类绝不可能以那种密度生活在地球的陆地表面。因此，今天的高出生率将会下降，

cues.en: today's low death rates will rise till they have exactly the same numerical value that will certainly be in a time short compared to seven eighty years.
cues.zh: 今天的低死亡率将会上升，直到它们的数值完全相等，这个时间与 780 年相比绝对是非常短暂的。

cues.en: So maybe you're wondering what sort of options are available if we wanted to address the problem.
cues.zh: 所以你可能会想，如果我们想解决这个问题，有哪些可选方案。

cues.en: In the left hand column I've listed some of things that we should encourage if we want to raise the rate of growth of population and in so doing make the problem worse.
cues.zh: 在左栏中，我列出了一些如果我们要提高人口增长率、从而让问题变得更糟时应当鼓励的事情。

cues.en: Just look at the list. Everything in the list is as sacred as motherhood.
cues.zh: 看看这份清单。清单上的每一项都像母性一样神圣不可侵犯。

cues.en: There's immigration,
cues.zh: 有移民，

cues.en: medicine, public health, sanitation.
cues.zh: 医药、公共卫生、环境卫生。

cues.en: These are all devoted to the humane goals of lowering the death rate. And that's very important to me if it's my death they're lowering.
cues.zh: 这些都致力于降低死亡率的人道目标。如果降低的是我的死亡率，那对我来说非常重要。

cues.en: But then I have to realize that anything that just lowers the death rate makes the population problem worse.
cues.zh: 但随后我必须意识到，任何仅仅降低死亡率的事情都会让人口问题变得更糟。

cues.en: There's peace,
cues.zh: 有和平，

cues.en: law and order.
cues.zh: 法律与秩序。

cues.en: Scientific agriculture has lowered the death rate due to famine. That just makes the population problem worse.
cues.zh: 科学农业降低了因饥荒导致的死亡率。那只会让人口问题变得更糟。

cues.en: The 55 miles per hour speed limit saved thousands of lives.
cues.zh: 每小时55英里的限速挽救了数千条生命。

cues.en: Makes the population problem worse. Clean air makes it worse.
cues.zh: 让人口问题变得更糟。清洁空气也让问题更糟。

cues.en: Now in this column are some of the things we should encourage if we want to lower the rate of growth population and in so doing help solve the population problem.
cues.zh: 现在这一栏里是一些如果我们要降低人口增长率、从而帮助解决人口问题时应当鼓励的事情。

cues.en: Well there's abstention,
cues.zh: 嗯，有节欲，

cues.en: contraception,
cues.zh: 避孕，

cues.en: abortion, small families,
cues.zh: 堕胎、小家庭，

cues.en: stop immigration,
cues.zh: 停止移民，

cues.en: disease, war, murder, famine, accidents.
cues.zh: 疾病、战争、谋杀、饥荒、事故。

cues.en: Now smoking clearly raises the death rate.
cues.zh: 吸烟显然会提高死亡率。

cues.en: Now that helps solve the problem.
cues.zh: 这有助于解决问题。

cues.en: Well, remember our conclusion from the cartoon of one person per square meter? We concluded that zero population growth is going to happen. Let's state that conclusion in other terms and say it's obvious nature is going to choose from the right hand list and we don't have to do anything
cues.zh: 还记得我们从那张每人一平方米的漫画中得出的结论吗？我们得出的结论是零人口增长终将发生。让我们用另一种方式表述这个结论：显然大自然会从右栏中选择，而我们什么都不用做，

cues.en: except be prepared to live with whatever nature chooses from that right hand list.
cues.zh: 只需准备好接受大自然从右栏中选出的任何结果。

cues.en: Or we can exercise the one option that's open to us.
cues.zh: 或者，我们可以做出摆在我们面前的那个选择。

cues.en: And that option
cues.zh: 而那个选择

cues.en: is to choose first from the right hand list. We've got to find something here we can go out and campaign for.
cues.zh: 就是先从右边的列表中挑选。我们得从中挑出一些能公开支持并倡导的事情。

cues.en: Anyone here for promoting disease?
cues.zh: 在座有人支持传播疾病吗？

cues.en: We now have the capability of incredible war. Would you like more murder, more famine, more accidents?
cues.zh: 我们现在具备了发动惊人战争的能力。你想要更多的谋杀、更多的饥荒、更多的事故吗？

cues.en: Here we can see the human dilemma
cues.zh: 在这里我们可以看到人类的困境

cues.en: because everything we regard as good makes the population problem worse.
cues.zh: 因为我们认为好的一切，都会让人口问题进一步恶化。

cues.en: Everything we regard as bad helps solve the problem.
cues.zh: 而我们认为坏的一切，却有助于解决这个问题。

cues.en: Now there is a dilemma if ever there was one.
cues.zh: 如果真有进退两难的困境，那这就是了。

cues.en: And the one remaining question is education. Does it go in the left hand column or the right hand column? Well, I'd have to say thus far it's been firmly in the left hand column and hasn't done much about reducing ignorance of the problem.
cues.zh: 剩下的唯一问题是教育。它该归到左边那列，还是右边那列？我得说，到目前为止它都牢牢属于左边那一列，在消除对该问题的无知上收效甚微。

cues.en: And nature is already choosing from that right hand list. You've read about the
cues.zh: 大自然已经在从右边那个列表中做选择了。大家都在新闻里读到过

cues.en: AIDS epidemic that's devastating the Continent Of Africa. I had a friend back from Zimbabwe.
cues.zh: 重创非洲大陆的艾滋病疫情。我有个朋友刚从津巴布韦回来。

cues.en: People, he said, are dying on the streets.
cues.zh: 他说，人们在大街上死去。

cues.en: Nature's taking care of the problem.
cues.zh: 大自然正在“解决”这个问题。

cues.en: So where do we start? Well, let's start in Boulder, Colorado.
cues.zh: 那我们从哪里开始？不妨从科罗拉多州的 Boulder 开始。

cues.en: Here's a graph of Boulder's population.
cues.zh: 这是 Boulder 的人口走势图。

cues.en: There's the 1950 US census figure, 1960,
cues.zh: 这是 1950 年美国人口普查的数据，这是 1960 年，

cues.en: In that twenty year period, the average growth rate of Boulder's population was about 6% per year. Now we've been able to slow the growth somewhat. There's a 2,000 census figure.
cues.zh: 在那 20 年间，Boulder 的年均人口增长率约为 6%。现在我们已经能在一定程度上减缓增长了。这是 2000 年的人口普查数据。

cues.en: Well, like to ask the people, let's start with a 2,000 census figure, go another
cues.zh: 那么，我想问大家，我们从2000年的人口普查数据开始，再过

cues.en: seventy years, one more human lifetime, and ask,
cues.zh: 七十年，也就是再经历一个人的一生，然后设问：

cues.en: what rate of growth of Boulder's population would we need in that seventy years so that at the end of seventy years, Boulder's population
cues.zh: 在未来的这七十年里，博尔德（Boulder）的人口需要达到怎样的增长率，才能在七十年结束时，

cues.en: would equal today's population of your choice of major American cities.
cues.zh: 其人口规模相当于你所选择的某个美国大城市的现代人口。

cues.en: Where Boulder in seventy years could be as big as Boston is today if we just grew 2.58%
cues.zh: 只要我们每年保持2.58%的增长率，

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 七十年后的博尔德就能达到今天波士顿的规模。

cues.en: Now if we thought Detroit was a better model, we'll have to shoot for 3.27%
cues.zh: 如果我们觉得底特律是一个更好的参照，那我们就得把目标定在每年

cues.en: per year.
And remember the historic figure on the preceding slide, 6% per year, if that could continue for one lifetime,
cues.zh: 再想想前面幻灯片上的历史数据——每年6%，如果这个速度能持续整整一代人的时间，

cues.en: Boulder would be larger than Los Angeles.
cues.zh: 博尔德就会比洛杉矶还要大。

cues.en: Now this isn't Boulder plus Broomfield, Lewisville, Lafayette, the other towns in the county. This was just Boulder.
cues.zh: 这可不是把博尔德加上布鲁姆菲尔德、路易斯维尔、拉斐特以及该县的其他城镇，这仅仅指博尔德本身。

cues.en: Well, it's obvious you couldn't put Los Angeles in the Boulder Valley. Therefore, it's obvious Boulder's population growth's gonna stop.
cues.zh: 很显然，你没法把洛杉矶塞进博尔德谷。因此，显而易见的是，博尔德的人口增长终究会停止。

cues.en: Now, the only question is,
cues.zh: 现在，唯一的问题是：

cues.en: will we be able to stop it while there's still some open space or will we wait until it's wall to wall people and we're all choking to death?
cues.zh: 我们是能在还留有一片开阔地时就将其煞住，还是非要等到到处挤满人、大家快要窒息的时候才罢休？

cues.en: Now it's interesting to read what the boosters say.
cues.zh: 看看那些城市推动者是怎么说的，挺有意思的。

cues.en: Some years ago we read that doubling its population in ten years, Boulder is indeed a stable community.
cues.zh: 几年前我们读到过，在十年内人口翻倍的博尔德，确实是一个稳定的社区。

cues.en: What in the world are they talking about? You're going a 100 miles an hour,
cues.zh: 这群人到底在说些什么？车速都开到每小时100英里了，

cues.en: 7% growth per year, doubling in less than ten years, and someone makes the idiotic statement that we're stable.
cues.zh: 每年7%的增长率，不到十年人口就要翻倍，居然有人会说出我们很稳定这种荒谬绝伦的话。

cues.en: We're standing still. We're not moving. They don't even understand
cues.zh: 我们停滞不前。我们没有行动。他们甚至不明白

cues.en: the meaning of the words that they put down on paper.
cues.zh: 他们写在纸上的那些词的含义。

cues.en: Well, every once in a while somebody says, but you know, a bigger city might be a better city. And I have to say, wait a minute,
cues.zh: 偶尔有人会说，你知道，更大的城市也许更好。我得说，等一下，

cues.en: we've already done that experiment, we don't need to wonder what will be the effect of growth on Boulder because Boulder tomorrow
cues.zh: 我们已经做过那个实验了，我们不需要去猜想增长对博尔德会有什么影响，因为明天的博尔德

cues.en: can be seen in Los Angeles today.
cues.zh: 可以从今天的洛杉矶看到。

cues.en: And for the price of an airplane ticket, we can step seventy years into the future and see exactly
cues.zh: 而只需一张机票的价钱，我们就能踏入七十年后的未来，看看

cues.en: what it's like.
cues.zh: 它到底是什么样子。

cues.en: And what is it like? Well, here's an interesting headline
cues.zh: 那是什么样子呢？这里有一条有趣的新闻标题

cues.en: from
cues.zh: 来自

cues.en: Los Angeles.
cues.zh: 洛杉矶。

cues.en: That headline probably has something to do with this headline.
cues.zh: 那条标题大概和这条标题有关。

cues.en: So,
cues.zh: 所以，

cues.en: well, how are we doing in Colorado?
cues.zh: 我们在科罗拉多做得怎么样？

cues.en: The Denver Post tells us that we're the growth capital of The USA and proud of it.
cues.zh: 《丹佛邮报》告诉我们，我们是美国的增长之都，而且引以为豪。

cues.en: The Rocky Mountain News tells us to expect another million people in the Front Range in the next twenty years.
cues.zh: 《落基山新闻》告诉我们要预计未来二十年前山地区还会增加一百万人。

cues.en: But in the post there was an interesting story. Someone was quoted as saying Colorado has a 3% growth rate. That's like a third world country with no birth control.
cues.zh: 但邮报里有篇有趣的报道。有人被引述说科罗拉多有3%的增长率。那就像一个没有节育的第三世界国家。

cues.en: We send foreign aid,
cues.zh: 我们送对外援助，

cues.en: family planning assistance to countries
cues.zh: 计划生育援助给那些

cues.en: that have smaller population growth rates than Colorado has.
cues.zh: 人口增长率比科罗拉多还低的国家。

cues.en: Well, as you can imagine,
cues.zh: 嗯，你可以想象，

cues.en: growth control is very controversial
cues.zh: 增长控制非常有争议

cues.en: and I treasure the letter from which these quotations are taken. Now, this letter was written to me by a leading citizen of this community.
cues.zh: 我很珍视这些引文所出自的那封信。这封信是本社区一位杰出公民写给我的。

cues.en: He's a leading proponent of controlled growth.
cues.zh: 他是有控制增长的主要倡导者。

cues.en: Now, controlled growth just means growth.
cues.zh: 所谓有控制增长，其实就是增长。

cues.en: This man writes: I take no exception to your arguments regarding exponential growth.
cues.zh: 这个人写道：我对你们关于指数增长的论点没有异议。

cues.en: I don't believe the exponential argument is valid at the local level.
cues.zh: 我不认为指数论点在局部层面是成立的。

cues.en: So you see, arithmetic doesn't hold in Boulder.
cues.zh: 所以你看，算术在博尔德不成立。

cues.en: Now, I have to admit that man has a degree from the University of Colorado.
cues.zh: 现在，我得承认，那个人拥有科罗拉多大学的学位。

cues.en: It's not a degree in mathematics,
cues.zh: 那不是数学学位，

cues.en: in science or in engineering.
cues.zh: 也不是科学或工程学位。

cues.en: Let's look now at what happens when we have this kind of steady growth in a finite environment.
cues.zh: 现在我们来看看，在有限环境中出现这种稳定增长时会发生什么。

cues.en: Bacteria grow by doubling and one bacterium divides to become two, the two divide to become four,
cues.zh: 细菌通过翻倍增长，一个细菌分裂成两个，两个分裂成四个，

cues.en: the four become eight, 16 and so on. Suppose we had bacteria that doubled in number this way every minute.
cues.zh: 四个变成八个、十六个，依此类推。假设我们有种细菌，每分钟数量就这样翻倍。

cues.en: Suppose we put one of these bacteria in an empty bottle at eleven in the morning and then observe that the bottle is full at twelve noon.
cues.zh: 假设我们在上午十一点把其中一个细菌放进一个空瓶子，然后观察到中午十二点时瓶子满了。

cues.en: Now there's our case of just ordinary,
cues.zh: 这就是我们所说的普通、

cues.en: steady growth.
cues.zh: 稳定增长的情况。

cues.en: It has a doubling time of one minute.
cues.zh: 它的倍增时间是一分钟。

cues.en: It's in the finite environment of one bottle.
cues.zh: 它处于一个瓶子的有限环境中。

cues.en: I want to ask you three questions.
cues.zh: 我想问你三个问题。

cues.en: Number one: At what time was the bottle half full?
cues.zh: 第一个：瓶子在什么时间半满？

cues.en: Well, would you believe 11:59,
cues.zh: 你信不信是11点59分，

cues.en: one minute before twelve, because they double in number every minute.
cues.zh: 也就是十二点前一分钟，因为它们的数量每分钟翻倍。

cues.en: And the second question:
cues.zh: 第二个问题：

cues.en: If you were an average bacterium in that bottle, at what time
cues.zh: 如果你是那个瓶子里的一个普通细菌，你会在什么时间

cues.en: would you first realize that you were running out of space?
cues.zh: 第一次意识到空间快用完了？

cues.en: Now think about this. This kind of steady growth is the centerpiece
cues.zh: 现在想想看。这种持续的增长正是

cues.en: of the national
cues.zh: 国家

cues.en: economy and of the entire global economy.
cues.zh: 经济乃至整个全球经济的核心。

cues.en: Think about it.
cues.zh: 好好想想吧。

cues.en: Well,

cues.zh: 他们估计，可能还能再开采三十年，之后在那里采煤

cues.en: to mine there. And then what will we do when we want to switch on the lights?
cues.zh: 就变得不经济了。到那时，我们想开灯该怎么办？

cues.en: Let's now go back and note that in the nineteen seventies, there was great national concern about energy,
cues.zh: 现在让我们回顾一下，上世纪七十年代，全国对能源问题高度关注，

cues.en: but this concern disappeared in the eighties.
cues.zh: 但这种关注在八十年代消失了。

cues.en: Now the concerns about energy in the seventies prompted experts,
cues.zh: 七十年代对能源的担忧促使专家、

cues.en: journalists and scientists
cues.zh: 记者和科学家

cues.en: to assure the American people that there was no reason to be concerned. So let's go back now and look at some of those assurances from the seventies
cues.zh: 向美国人民保证，没有理由担心。那么让我们回到过去，看看七十年代的那些保证

cues.en: so we can see what to expect
cues.zh: 这样我们就能预见到

cues.en: as the energy crisis returns.
cues.zh: 当能源危机再次来临时会发生什么。

cues.en: Here is the director of the Energy Division of the Oak Ridge National Laboratories.
cues.zh: 这里是橡树岭国家实验室能源部的主任。

cues.en: He's telling us how expensive it is to import oil,
cues.zh: 他告诉我们进口石油成本有多高，

cues.en: telling us we must have big increases in our use of coal. Under these conditions, he estimates America's coal reserves are so huge they could last a minimum of three hundred years, probably a maximum of a thousand years.
cues.zh: 并告诉我们必须大幅增加煤炭的使用。在这种情况下，他估计美国的煤炭储量极其巨大，至少可以维持三百年，最多可能达到一千年。

cues.en: Now you've just seen the facts.
cues.zh: 现在你们刚刚看到了事实。

cues.en: Now you see what an expert tells us and what can you conclude?
cues.zh: 现在你们看到了专家的说法，你们能得出什么结论？

cues.en: There was a three hour television special on CBS on energy. The reporter said by the lowest estimate we have enough coal for two hundred years, but the highest enough for more than a thousand years.
cues.zh: 哥伦比亚广播公司（CBS）曾播出一场关于能源的三小时电视特别节目。记者说，根据最低估计，我们的煤炭够用两百年，但最高估计则超过一千年。

cues.en: You've just seen the facts.
cues.zh: 你们刚刚看到了事实。

cues.en: Now you see what a journalist tells us after careful study.
cues.zh: 现在你们看到了记者经过仔细研究后的说法。

cues.en: And what can you conclude?
cues.zh: 你们能得出什么结论？

cues.en: In the Journal of Chemical Education, on the page for high school chemistry teachers,
cues.zh: 在《化学教育期刊》上，面向高中化学教师的版块里，

cues.en: an article written by the scientific
cues.zh: 有一篇由该期刊科学

cues.en: staff of the journal,
cues.zh: 工作人员撰写的文章，

cues.en: we read that our proved coal reserves are enormous and they give a figure. These could satisfy present US energy needs for nearly a thousand years.
cues.zh: 我们读到，我们已探明的煤炭储量巨大，并给出了一个数字。这些储量可以满足美国当前近一千年的能源需求。

cues.en: Let's do long division. You take the coal they say is there, divide by what was then the current rate of consumption
cues.zh: 我们来做个长除法。你用他们说的那里的煤炭总量，除以当时的当前消耗速率，

cues.en: you get a hundred and eighty years.
cues.zh: 你得到的数字是一百八十年。

cues.en: Now they didn't say current rate of consumption, they said present US energy needs.
cues.zh: 然而他们说的不是当前的消耗速率，而是说美国当前的能源需求。

cues.en: Coal today supplies about one fifth, around 20% of the energy that we use in this country. So if you'd like to calculate how long this quantity of coal could satisfy present US energy needs,
cues.zh: 如今煤炭供应了我们国家所使用能源的大约五分之一，即20%左右。所以，如果你想计算这些数量的煤炭能满足美国当前能源需求多久，

cues.en: you have to multiply this denominator by five. When you do that, you get thirty six years. They said nearly a thousand years.
cues.zh: 你必须将这个分母乘以五。当你这么做时，你得到的是三十六年。而他们说的是近一千年。

cues.en: Newsweek magazine and a cover story on energy said at present rates of consumption,
cues.zh: 《新闻周刊》杂志有一篇关于能源的封面报道说，按目前的消耗速度，

cues.en: we have enough coal for six hundred and sixty six point five years.
cues.zh: 我们的煤还够用六百六十六点五年。

cues.en: And the point five means they think it'll run out in July instead of January.
cues.zh: 而那个"点五"的意思是，他们认为煤会在七月而不是一月耗尽。

cues.en: Now, if you round that off and say roughly six hundred years,
cues.zh: 现在，如果把它取整，说大约六百年，

cues.en: 600 is close enough to 500 to lie within the uncertainty of our knowledge of the size of the resource. So with that observation,
cues.zh: 600已经足够接近500，落在我们对这种资源储量认知的不确定性范围之内。基于这个观察，

cues.en: that is a correct statement. At present rates, meaning zero growth, we have enough coal for around six hundred years.
cues.zh: 这句话是对的。按目前的速度，也就是零增长，我们的煤大约还够用六百年。

cues.en: The whole point of the story that this led into was that we have to have rapid growth in coal consumption in The United States. Now it's obvious, isn't it, if you have the growth they're writing about, it won't last as long as they said it would last with zero growth.
cues.zh: 这篇报道引出的故事的核心观点是，美国的煤炭消耗必须快速增长。这很明显，对吧？如果真有他们所写的那种增长，煤就不会像他们所说的零增长情况下那样持久了。

cues.en: They never mentioned this. I wrote them a long letter, told them I thought this was a serious representation
cues.zh: 他们从未提到这一点。我给他们写了一封长信，告诉他们我认为这是一种严重的失实陈述，

cues.en: give the readers the feeling that we can have all the growth that they're writing about and still have coal around for 650.
cues.zh: 会让读者觉得我们既可以实现他们所写的那种增长，煤还能撑到六百五十年后。

cues.en: I got back a nice form letter. It had nothing to do with what I tried to explain to them.
cues.zh: 我收到了一封客套的格式回信，和我试图向他们解释的内容毫无关系。

cues.en: I gave this talk at a high school in Omaha and after the talk the high school physics teacher came to me and he had a booklet. Said, Have you seen this? I hadn't seen it. He said, Look at this.
cues.zh: 我在奥马哈的一所高中做过这个演讲，演讲结束后，那所高中的物理老师找到我，手里拿着一本小册子。他说：你看过这个吗？我没看过。他说：看看这个。

cues.en: We've got coal coming out of our ears.
cues.zh: 我们手头的煤炭多得都快溢出来了。

cues.en: As reported by Forbes Magazine, now that's a prominent business magazine,
cues.zh: 正如《福布斯》杂志所报道的那样，这可是一本知名的商业杂志，

cues.en: The United States has 437,000,000,000
tons of known coal reserves. That is a good figure.
cues.zh: 吨已探明的煤炭储量。这是一个相当可观的数字。

cues.en: This is equivalent to a lot of BTUs
cues.zh: 这相当于大量的英热单位，

cues.en: or it's enough energy to keep 100,000,000
cues.zh: 或者说，这些能量足够让 100,000,000 座

cues.en: large electric generating plants going for the next eight hundred years or so. Now the teacher said to me, How can that be true?
cues.zh: 大型发电厂再运转大约八百年。当时那位老师问我，这怎么可能是真的呢？

cues.en: That's one large electric generating plant for every two people in The United States.
cues.zh: 相当于美国每两个人就拥有一座大型发电厂。

cues.en: I said, of course it can't be true. It's absolute nonsense.
cues.zh: 我说，这当然不可能是真的。简直是一派胡言。

cues.en: Let's do long division to see how crazy it is. So you take the coal, they say is there, divide by what was then the current rate of consumption, find you couldn't keep that rate up for eight hundred years. We hardly have 500 large electric generating plants. They said it would be good for a 100,000,000
cues.zh: 我们用长除法算算看它有多离谱。拿他们说存在的煤炭总量，除以当时实际的消耗速率，就会发现根本无法维持八百年。我们甚至连 500 座大型发电厂都凑不齐。而他们却说这足够支撑 100,000,000 座

cues.en: such plants.
cues.zh: 这样的发电厂。

cues.en: Time Magazine tells us that beneath the pits heads of Appalachia and the Ohio Valley and under the sprawling strip mines of the West, lie coal seams rich enough to meet the country's power needs for centuries
cues.zh: 《时代周刊》告诉我们，在阿巴拉契亚山脉和俄亥俄河谷的井口之下，以及西部广袤的露天煤矿之下，蕴藏着足以满足该国几个世纪电力需求的丰富煤层，

cues.en: no matter how much energy consumption may grow.
cues.zh: 无论能源消耗增长多么迅猛。

cues.en: And so I give you a very fundamental observation. Don't believe any prediction
cues.zh: 因此，我向大家提出一个非常基础的观察结论：不要相信任何关于

cues.en: of the life expectancy of a nonrenewable resource until you have confirmed the prediction by repeating the calculation.
cues.zh: 不可再生资源开采寿命的预测，除非你亲自重复计算并证实了该预测。

cues.en: As a corollary, we have to note that the more optimistic the prediction, the greater is the probability
cues.zh: 由此推论，我们必须指出，预测越是乐观，

cues.en: that it's based on faulty arithmetic or on no arithmetic
cues.zh: 其基于错误算术、甚至完全没有算术依据的

cues.en: at all.
cues.zh: 概率就越大。

cues.en: Again from Time Magazine,
cues.zh: 同样摘自《时代周刊》，

cues.en: energy industries agree that to achieve some form of energy self sufficiency,
cues.zh: 能源行业一致认为，为了实现某种形式的能源自给自足，

cues.en: The US must mine all the coal that it can.
cues.zh: 美国必须尽可能开采所有的煤炭。

cues.en: Now think about that for just a moment.
cues.zh: 现在大家思考一下这个说法。

cues.en: Let me paraphrase it.
cues.zh: 让我换种说法来解释。

cues.en: The more rapidly we consume our resources, the more self sufficient we'll be.
cues.zh: 我们消耗资源的节奏越快，我们就会越自给自足。

cues.en: Now isn't that what it says?
cues.zh: 这不正是它所表达的意思吗？

cues.en: Well, David Brower called this the policy of strength through exhaustion.
cues.zh: 嗯，David Brower 把这称为“通过枯竭获得力量”的政策。

cues.en: Now here's an example of strength through exhaustion.
cues.zh: 现在这里就有一个“通过枯竭获得力量”的例子。

cues.en: Here is William Simon, energy advisor to the President of The United States.
cues.zh: 这位是 William Simon，美国总统的能源顾问。

cues.en: Simon says we should be trying to get as many holes drilled as possible to get the proven oil reserves.
cues.zh: Simon 表示，我们应该尽最大努力钻探尽可能多的油井，以获取已探明的石油储量。

cues.en: The more rapidly we can get the last of that oil up out of the ground and finish using it,
cues.zh: 我们越快把地下最后残存的石油抽上来并用完，

cues.en: the better off we'll be.
cues.zh: 我们的处境就会越好。

cues.en: Well, let's look at Doctor. Hubbard's graph for oil production in the Lower 48 states. There was a long period of approximately
cues.zh: 好吧，让我们来看看哈伯德博士关于美国本土48州石油产量的图表。这里有一个长期的、大约是

cues.en: steady growth indicated by this straight line on the semi logarithmic plot.
cues.zh: 稳步增长的时期，半对数坐标图上的这条直线就表明了这一点。

cues.en: But for quite a while, production has fallen below the growth curve while our demand continued on up this growth curve until the nineteen seventies.
cues.zh: 但有一段时间，产量一直落后于增长曲线，而我们的需求却沿着这条增长曲线持续上升，一直持续到20世纪70年代。

cues.en: Now, it's obvious the difference between those two curves has to be made up with imports
cues.zh: 现在，很显然这两条曲线之间的差额只能靠进口来弥补，

cues.en: and it was in early nineteen ninety five
cues.zh: 正是在1995年初，

cues.en: that the news told us that the year '94
cues.zh: 新闻告诉我们，94年

cues.en: was the first year in our nation's history in which we had to import more oil than we were able to get out of our own ground.
cues.zh: 是我们国家历史上第一年，我们进口的石油超过了我们从本土开采出来的石油。

cues.en: Well, maybe you're wondering, does it make any sense to imagine that we could have steady growth in the rate of consumption of a resource till the last bit of it was used and then the rate of consumption would plunge abruptly to zero?
cues.zh: 也许你在想，设想一种资源的消耗速率保持稳定增长，直到最后一点被用完，然后消耗速率突然骤降到零，这有意义吗？

cues.en: I say, no, that does not make sense. You say, alright, why bother us then with the calculation of this expiration time?
cues.zh: 我说，不，这没有意义。你说，那好，那为什么还要费心计算这个耗尽时间呢？

cues.en: My answer is this: every segment of our society, our business leaders, government leaders, political leaders, the local level, state level, national level, everyone aspires
cues.zh: 我的回答是：我们社会的每一个部分，商界领袖、政府领袖、政治领袖，地方层面、州层面、国家层面，每个人都渴望

cues.en: to maintain a society in which all measures of material consumption continue to grow steadily
cues.zh: 维持这样一个社会：所有物质消费指标都持续稳定增长

cues.en: year after year after year, world without end.
cues.zh: 年复一年，永无止境。

cues.en: Now since that's so central to everything we do, we ought to know where it would lead.
cues.zh: 既然这对我们做的一切如此核心，我们理应知道它会导向何方。

cues.en: On the other hand, we should recognize there is a better model. We turn again to the work of the late Doctor. Hubbard. He has plotted the rate of consumption of resources that have already expired. He finds, yes, there is an early period of steady growth in the rate of consumption
cues.zh: 另一方面，我们应该认识到存在一个更好的模型。我们再次回到已故的Hubbard博士的工作。他绘制了已经耗尽的资源的消耗速率。他发现，是的，早期确实有一段消耗速率稳定增长的时期

cues.en: but then the rate goes through a maximum and comes back down in a nice symmetric bell shaped curve. And when he fitted this curve to the data on US oil production back in the nineteen seventies, he found that at that point we were right about there. We were one halfway
cues.zh: 但随后速率经过一个最大值，再以漂亮的对称钟形曲线回落。当他用这条曲线拟合上世纪七十年代美国石油产量的数据时，他发现当时我们正好处在那里。我们正走完一半

cues.en: through
cues.zh: 的

cues.en: that enormous resource.
cues.zh: 那巨大资源。

cues.en: Now that's roughly what that Texas expert said in the quotation we saw earlier.
cues.zh: 刚才我们看到的引文大致就是那位得克萨斯专家所说的。

cues.en: Now let's see what it means.
cues.zh: 现在我们来看看这意味着什么。

cues.en: It means that from now on domestic oil production can only go downhill and it's downhill all the rest of the way.
cues.zh: 这意味着从今往后，国内石油产量只能走下坡路，而且之后一路都是下坡。

cues.en: And it doesn't matter what they say inside the Beltway in Washington DC.
cues.zh: 不管华盛顿特区环城公路内的人怎么说，都无关紧要。

cues.en: Now it means we could work hard and put some bumps on the downhill side of the curve. You'll see there are bumps on the uphill side.
cues.zh: 这意味着我们可以努力干活，在下坡段弄出一些起伏。你会看到上坡段本来就有起伏。

cues.en: The debate is heating up over drilling in the Arctic Wildlife Refuge.
cues.zh: 关于在北极野生动物保护区钻探的争论正愈演愈烈。

cues.en: I've seen the estimate that they might find 3,200,000,000
cues.zh: 我看到过估计说他们可能在那里找到32亿

cues.en: barrels of oil up there.
cues.zh: 桶石油。

cues.en: is the area of that little tiny square
cues.zh: 就是那个小方块代表的面积

cues.en: that's less than one year's consumption in The United States.
cues.zh: 还不到美国一年的消耗量。

cues.en: Now, let's look at the curve in this way. The area under the entire curve represents
cues.zh: 现在，我们这样来看这条曲线。整条曲线下方的面积代表

cues.en: the entire resource of US petroleum
cues.zh: 美国石油的全部资源

cues.en: before any of it was used.
cues.zh: 在任何一点被使用之前。

cues.en: Now, that area has been divided here into three parts. Unshaded on the left, that's the oil we've taken from the ground. We've used it, it's gone.
cues.zh: 现在，这个面积在这里被分成三部分。左边未阴影的部分，是我们已经从地下采出的石油。我们已经用掉了，它没了。

cues.en: This vertical shaded band, that's the oil we've drilled into. We found it. We're pumping on it today.
cues.zh: 这条竖直的阴影带，是我们已经钻探到的石油。我们找到了它。我们今天正在抽它。

cues.en: Shaded in green on the right is the undiscovered oil. We have very good ways now of estimating how much oil remains undiscovered.
cues.zh: 右边绿色阴影是未探明的石油。我们现在有非常好的方法来估计还有多少石油未被探明。

cues.en: This is the undiscovered oil. This is the oil we're looking for in all those places where drilling is going on. This is the oil we've got to find if we're going to make it down the curve on schedule.
cues.zh: 这就是未探明的石油。这就是我们在所有正在进行钻探的地方寻找的石油。如果我们要按计划沿曲线走下去，这就是我们必须找到的石油。

cues.en: Now, every once in while someone reminds me that a hundred years ago someone did a calculation
cues.zh: 每隔一段时间，总有人提醒我，一百年前有人做过一项计算

cues.en: and predicted that The US would be out of oil perhaps in twenty five years. We obviously were not. The calculation must have been wrong. Therefore, of course, all calculations are wrong.
cues.zh: 并预测美国也许会在二十五年后石油枯竭。我们显然没有。那个计算肯定错了。所以，当然，所有计算都是错的。

cues.en: Well, now let's understand what they did a hundred years ago.
cues.zh: 好，现在我们来了解一下他们一百年前是怎么做的。

cues.en: This band of discovered oil a hundred years ago was way over in here someplace.
cues.zh: 一百年前发现的这条石油带，就在这一带某个地方。

cues.en: At that point, they had no idea how much oil was undiscovered.
cues.zh: 当时，他们完全不知道还有多少石油未被发现。

cues.en: So they just took the discovered oil divided by how rapidly it was then being consumed, come up with twenty five years. Now it's clear, you have to make a new calculation every time you make a new discovery.
cues.zh: 所以他们直接用已探明的石油储量除以当时的消耗速度，算出了25年。但很显然，每当有新发现时，你都得重新算一遍。

cues.en: We're not asking today how long will the discovered oil last. We're asking about the discovered and the undiscovered.
cues.zh: 今天我们不是在问已探明的石油还能用多久，而是在问已探明和未探明的总量。

cues.en: We're now asking about the rest of the oil. And what does the geological survey tell us? Back in 1984,
cues.zh: 我们现在要问的是剩下的石油。地质调查告诉了我们什么？早在1984年，

cues.en: they said that the estimated supply in The US from undiscovered resources and demonstrated reserves
cues.zh: 他们提到美国未发现资源和已探明储量的估计供应量

cues.en: is thirty six years at present rates of production or nineteen years in the absence of imports.
cues.zh: 按目前的生产速度是三十六年，如果没有进口则是十九年。

cues.en: Five years later in 1989,
cues.zh: 五年后的1989年，

cues.en: that thirty six years is down to thirty two years. The nineteen years is down to sixteen years. So the numbers are holding together as we march down the right hand side of the Hubbard curve.
cues.zh: 那36年降到了32年。19年降到了16年。所以当我们沿着Hubbard曲线右侧往下走时，这些数字是对得上的。

cues.en: So maybe you're wondering, well, why didn't somebody tell us this?
cues.zh: 也许你会纳闷，为什么没人早点告诉我们？

cues.en: It was back in 1956,
Doctor. Hubbard addressed a convention of petroleum geologists and engineers. He told them that his calculations
cues.zh: Hubbard 博士在一次石油地质学家和工程师大会上发言。他告诉大家，他的计算

cues.en: led him to conclude that the peaks of US oil and gas production that you just saw can be expected to occur between 1966
cues.zh: 让他得出结论：大家刚才看到的美国油气产量峰值，预计会出现在 1966 年
到 1971 年之间。

cues.en: No one took him seriously.
cues.zh: 当时没人把他的话当回事。

cues.en: So let's see what's happened. The data here are from the Department of Energy.
cues.zh: 那我们来看看后来发生了什么。这些数据来自美国能源部。

cues.en: So this is US oil production. We see a long period of approximately steady growth.
cues.zh: 这是美国的石油产量。可以看到一段相当漫长且大致平稳的增长期。

cues.en: Here's the year 1956
cues.zh: 这里是 1956 年，

cues.en: when Doctor. Hubbard did his analysis
cues.zh: 也就是 Hubbard 博士做出分析的那一年，

cues.en: and he said at that time that peak would occur between 1966
cues.zh: 他当时就预言峰值会出现在 1966 年
到 1971 年之间。

cues.en: Well, the peak occurred in 1970.
cues.zh: 结果，峰值确实出现在了 1970 年。

cues.en: It was followed by a very rapid decline.
cues.zh: 紧接着就是急剧的下滑。

cues.en: Then the Alaska pipeline started delivering its first oil and there was a partial recovery.
cues.zh: 随后 Alaska 管线开始输送首批石油，产量曾出现局部回升。

cues.en: That production has now peaked and everything's going downhill in unison
cues.zh: 但如今那里的产量也已见顶，所有的产油区都在同步下滑，

cues.en: and when I go to a spreadsheet on my computer at home
cues.zh: 当我在家里的电脑上打开电子表格，

cues.en: and I find the parameters of the curve that is the best fit to these scattered US data, from that best fit curve, it looks to me as though we have consumed
cues.zh: 寻找与这些分散的美国数据最佳拟合的曲线参数时，从那条最佳拟合曲线来看，我们似乎已经消耗了

cues.en: three quarters of the recoverable oil that was ever in our ground and we're now coasting downhill
cues.zh: 地下曾经拥有的全部可采石油的四分之三，如今我们正一路走低，

cues.en: on that last 25%
cues.zh: 消耗着最后 25%

cues.en: of the oil.
cues.zh: 的石油。

cues.zh: 那么，我们不禁要问：美国能源部对此有何作为？

cues.en: And here in 1998,
we read about a new comprehensive national energy strategy, a set of policy goals that include
cues.zh: 我们看到了一项新的国家综合能源战略，其中包含一系列政策目标，包括

cues.en: halting the slide
cues.zh: 遏制住

cues.en: in US oil production
cues.zh: 美国石油产量的下滑势头，

cues.en: by the year 2005.
cues.zh: 时间定在 2005 年之前。

cues.en: Now ask yourself, what do you think is the chance that we can do anything more than put a little bump on the downhill side of the curve.
cues.zh: 现在问问你自己，你觉得我们除了在这条曲线下坡段弄出个小凸起之外，还能做更多事情的概率有多大？

cues.en: Well, what does this mean?
cues.zh: 那么，这意味着什么呢？

cues.en: Let's look at the definition of modern agriculture.
cues.zh: 让我们看看现代农业的定义。

cues.en: It's the use of land to convert petroleum into food.
cues.zh: 就是利用土地把石油转化为食物。

cues.en: And we can see the end of the petroleum.
cues.zh: 而我们可以看到石油的终结。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: we have to ask about world petroleum.
cues.zh: 我们得问问世界石油的情况。

cues.en: And in 1972,
Doctor. Hubbard produced this curve and he suggested that he thought the peak of world production would occur around 1995.
cues.zh: 哈伯特博士制作了这条曲线，他提出他认为世界石油产量的峰值会出现在1995年左右。

cues.en: So we have to go to the data and see what has happened.
cues.zh: 所以我们得去看数据，看看实际发生了什么。

cues.en: Here, again, from our Department of Energy, but this now is world oil production
cues.zh: 这里同样来自我们的能源部，但现在是世界石油产量

cues.en: and we can see a long period of steady growth of oil production. There was quite a major drop right there. Then there was a recovery then as simply an enormous drop and a partial recovery here. So it's clear we're not yet over the peak. Each of those drops that you saw there was due to a price hike from OPEC and I think that those drops in delaying the arrival of the peak are the reason for the fact that the peak will occur later than Doctor. Hubbard had projected it to be. Well, I go back to my spreadsheet on my computer at home and now, in addition to just fitting the curve, since the curve has not started down, I can't get a very good fit for the curve for the area under the curve. But what I have to do then is to go to the geology literature
cues.zh: 我们可以看到石油产量经历了很长一段时间的稳定增长。那里有一个相当大的下降。然后有一次恢复，接着是一次巨大的下降，这里又部分恢复。所以很明显我们还没有过峰值。你看到的每一次下降都是由于OPEC的提价，而我认为这些下降推迟了峰值的到来，这就是峰值会比哈伯特博士预测的晚出现的原因。那么，我回到我家电脑上的电子表格，现在，除了拟合曲线之外，由于曲线还没有开始下降，我无法很好地拟合曲线下方的面积。但我接下来要做的是去查阅地质学文献

cues.en: and find out what is the consensus
cues.zh: 找出地质学家们的共识

cues.en: figure among geologists
cues.zh: 数字是多少

cues.en: as to the total amount of oil we'll ever find on this earth.
cues.zh: 关于我们在这颗地球上最终能找到的石油总量。

cues.en: Well, this consensus figure is 2,000
cues.zh: 嗯，这个共识数字是 2000

cues.en: barrels.
cues.zh: 桶。

cues.en: Now, that's uncertain. It has an uncertainty, maybe 40%,
cues.zh: 现在，这还不确定。它存在不确定性，可能40%，

cues.en: plus or minus 40. That's a very uncertain figure. But that's the consensus figure. If I do that and do the fit,
cues.zh: 正负40。这是个非常不确定的数字。但这是共识数字。如果我这么做并进行拟合，

cues.en: there is a curve.
cues.zh: 有一条曲线。

cues.en: The curve has a peak in the year 2004.
cues.zh: 这条曲线在2004年有一个峰值。

cues.en: Now, if I
cues.zh: 现在，如果我

cues.en: say, let's assume there's 50% more oil than the geology consensus,
cues.zh: 比如说，假设石油储量比地质学界共识多出50%，

cues.en: then the FIT gives me the year 2019
cues.zh: 然后FIT给出了2019年

cues.en: for the peak and if I assume there's twice as much oil as the consensus figure, then the peak's back to the year 2030.
cues.zh: 对于峰值，如果我假设石油储量是共识数字的两倍，那么峰值就回到了2030年。

cues.en: Now look at those curves.
cues.zh: 现在来看看那些曲线。

cues.en: In your life expectancy,
cues.zh: 在你预期寿命内，

cues.en: you are going to see
cues.zh: 你会看到

cues.en: the peak of world oil production. And you've got to ask yourself,
cues.zh: 世界石油产量的峰值。你得问问自己，

cues.en: what's life going to be like on this earth
cues.zh: 地球上的生活会变成什么样？

cues.en: when we have production declining
cues.zh: 当我们产量下降时

cues.en: and we have a growing population
cues.zh: 而且我们的人口还在不断增长

cues.en: and a growing per capita demand for oil? Now just think about it. This isn't rocket science. This is something that we can all think about. In the March issue of Scientific
cues.zh:
以及不断增长的人均石油需求？
现在想想看。
这不是什么高深的事。
这是我们都能思考的问题。
在《Scientific》三月刊中

cues.en: American for the year 1998,
cues.zh: 1998年的美国，

cues.en: there was a major article by two real petroleum geologists.
cues.zh: 有一篇重要文章，作者是两位真正的石油地质学家。

cues.en: One's in England, one's in France.
cues.zh: 一个在英国，一个在法国。

cues.en: They said that their estimate for this peak was that it would occur before
cues.zh: 他们说，他们估计这个峰值会在此之前出现

cues.en: the year 2010.
So their estimate and the one I'm showing you here that I've made, these are in the same ballpark
cues.zh: 所以他们的估算和我在这里展示的估算，大致在同一量级

cues.en: and we're talking about the same kind of numbers.
cues.zh: 我们说的是同一类数字。

cues.en: Now that analysis that was in Scientific American caused a lot of discussion
cues.zh: 发表在 Scientific American 上的那篇分析，引发了大量讨论

cues.en: and in particular in Fortune Magazine
cues.zh: 尤其是在《财富》杂志中

cues.en: commenting on this scientific analysis that was done by petroleum geologists,
cues.zh: 评论这份由石油地质学家完成的科学分析，

cues.en: we find an emeritus professor of economics at MIT saying that this analysis is a piece of foolishness.
cues.zh: 我们发现，MIT的一位经济学荣誉退休教授说，这项分析纯属无稽之谈。

cues.en: The world will never run out of oil, not in ten thousand years.
cues.zh: 世界永远不会耗尽石油，一万年后也不会。

cues.en: And so we have non scientists telling us that petroleum reserves are greater than ever before in history and we have geologists telling us that we're finding only one barrel of new oil for every four barrels we take out of the ground and consume.
cues.zh: 于是，非科学家告诉我们石油储量比历史上任何时候都多；而地质学家告诉我们，每从地下开采并消耗四桶油，只发现一桶新油。

cues.en: What is going on here?
cues.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

cues.en: You've seen the figures.
cues.zh: 你已经看过那些数字了。

cues.en: Here in 1999,
US Lower 48 State January oil output hit a fifty year low exactly what you expect as you're going down the right hand side of the Hubbert curve.
cues.zh: 美国本土48州1月石油产量创下50年新低，这正是沿着Hubbert曲线右侧下行时你会预期的情况。

cues.en: And one of Doctor. Hubbert's favorite graphs is this one. This is on a time scale from five thousand years ago to five thousand years in the future and the age fossil fuels is a little blip in the middle of the screen.
cues.zh: Hubbert博士最喜欢的图表之一就是这张。它的时间尺度从五千年前到五千年后，而化石燃料时代只是屏幕中间的一个小点。

cues.en: Think about it.
cues.zh: 想一想吧。

cues.en: Well, we have to ask about new discoveries.
cues.zh: 那么，我们得问问新发现的情况。

cues.en: Here in 1993,
we read about the largest oil discovery in The Gulf Mexico in the past twenty years,
cues.zh: 我们读到墨西哥湾过去20年最大的石油发现，

cues.en: an estimated 700,000,000
cues.zh: 估计有7亿

cues.en: barrels of oil. Now, that's a lot of oil,
cues.zh: 桶石油。现在，这可是一大笔石油，

cues.en: but a lot compared to what?
cues.zh: 但跟什么相比算多呢？

cues.en: At that point, we were consuming in The United States 16,600,000
cues.zh: 当时，美国每天消耗1660万

cues.en: barrels of oil every day.
cues.zh: 桶石油。

cues.en: Do the long division and you find that entire discovery would serve our needs for forty two days.
cues.zh: 算一下除法就知道，整个发现只够我们42天的需求。

cues.en: And that's the biggest discovery
cues.zh: 而这还是最大的发现

cues.en: they've made in the Gulf Of Mexico in twenty years.
cues.zh: 是他们在墨西哥湾20年里做出的。

cues.en: On the front page of the Wall Street Journal in 1997,
cues.zh: 1997年《华尔街日报》头版，

cues.en: we read about the new Hibernia oil field off the South Coast Of Newfoundland.
cues.zh: 我们读到了纽芬兰南海岸外的Hibernia新油田。

cues.en: Please note this one line in the headline. Now it will last fifty
cues.zh: 请注意标题里的这一行。现在它会持续五十年

cues.en: years.
cues.zh: 年。

cues.en: And let's go to that story in the Wall Street Journal and read about the Hibernia field.
cues.zh: 我们来看《华尔街日报》上的那篇报道，读一读关于Hibernia油田的内容。

cues.en: It's one of the largest oil discoveries in North America in decades.
cues.zh: 这是北美几十年来最大的石油发现之一。

cues.en: It should deliver its first oil by the end of the year. At least 20 more fields may follow offering well over a billion barrels of high quality crude promising a steady flow of oil will be just a quick tanker run away from the energy thirsty East Coast.
cues.zh: 它应该在年底前产出第一批石油。后续至少还有20多个油田，可能提供远超10亿桶的高品质原油，这意味着稳定的石油供应离能源饥渴的东海岸只有一趟油轮的距离。

cues.en: They may find billion barrels of oil in that undersea deposit.
cues.zh: 他们可能会在那片海底矿床中发现10亿桶石油。

cues.en: So a billion barrels, we are now consuming something like 18,000,000
cues.zh: 所以是10亿桶，而我们现在每天消耗大约1800万

cues.en: barrels a day. Do the long division
cues.zh: 桶。做个长除法

cues.en: and that whole supply would meet our needs in The United States for fifty six days.
cues.zh: 整个供应量只能满足美国五十六天的需求。

cues.en: And what did that headline say?
cues.zh: 那个标题说了什么？

cues.en: It said fifty years?
cues.zh: 它说的是五十年？

cues.en: Well, some people say there's nothing to worry about. And here we have a very prominent figure who says that we should
cues.zh: 好吧，有些人说没什么可担心的。而这里有一位非常显赫的人物说，我们应该

cues.en: grow corn, distill it into ethanol and we can run the entire fleet of US vehicles on ethanol derived from corn. And in support of this, he says, today ethanol production displaces over 43 a half million barrels of imported oil annually.
cues.zh: 种玉米，把它蒸馏成乙醇，我们就能让美国全部车辆都靠玉米制乙醇行驶。为了支持这一点，他说，如今乙醇产量每年替代超过4350万桶进口石油。

cues.en: Now, that sounds pretty good
cues.zh: 听起来相当不错

cues.en: until you think.
cues.zh: 直到你仔细想想。

cues.en: Now, the first thing that you have to do is to ask, okay, 43 and a half million. What fraction is that of the annual consumption of petroleum and vehicles in The United States? And the answer is it's 1%.
cues.zh: 首先你得问，好吧，4350万。这是美国石油和车辆年消费量的多大比例？答案是1%。

cues.en: You'd have to multiply corn production devoted to ethanol by a factor of 100
cues.zh: 你得把用于制造乙醇的玉米产量提高 100 倍

cues.en: just to make the numbers come out right. And I've seen the suggestion that that would take all the remaining... All of the agricultural land in The United States.
cues.zh: 才能让数据对得上。而且我看到有人建议说，这会占用所有剩下的……美国所有的农业用地。

cues.en: Now, the second problem is it takes diesel fuel to plow the ground to plant the corn.
cues.zh: 好了，第二个问题是，耕地种玉米需要消耗柴油。

cues.en: It takes fossil fuels to make the fertilizer to make the corn grow. It takes more diesel fuel to tend the corn and to harvest the corn. It takes more energy to do the distillation.
cues.zh: 生产让玉米生长的化肥需要化石燃料。照料和收割玉米需要更多的柴油。进行蒸馏还需要更多的能量。

cues.en: You finally get a gallon of ethanol.
cues.zh: 你最终得到了一加仑乙醇。

cues.en: You will be lucky if there's as much energy in the gallon of ethanol as it took to produce it.
cues.zh: 这一加仑乙醇里含有的能量，能不能比生产它所耗费的能量多，都得看运气。

cues.en: It's a loser.
cues.zh: 这根本是赔本买卖。

cues.en: Yet, this guy says don't worry,
cues.zh: 然而，这家伙却说别担心，

cues.en: everything will be alright.
cues.zh: 一切都会好起来的。

cues.en: Well,
cues.zh: 那么，

cues.en: there's a lesson here and the lesson is that we cannot let other people do our thinking for us.
cues.zh: 这里有个教训，那就是我们不能让别人替我们思考。

cues.en: Let's take another look at world oil production.
cues.zh: 让我们再来看看世界石油产量。

cues.en: Now, the graph here is slightly different from the one I showed earlier. What I'm showing here is per capita production
cues.zh: 现在，这里的图表和我之前展示的略有不同。我在这里展示的是人均产量

cues.en: of oil,
cues.zh: 石油，

cues.en: which means that at every point I take the world production divided by the world population that year.
cues.zh: 这意味着在每一个时间点，我都用当年的世界总产量除以世界总人口。

cues.en: Now the scale here on the vertical axis is liters per person each day.
cues.zh: 现在，这里纵轴的刻度是每人每天的升数。

cues.en: There's the number two. Now, two liters a person a day, two liters is about half a gallon.
cues.zh: 这里是数字二。现在，每人每天两升，两升大约是半加仑。

cues.en: Now, notice that the peak occurred in the nineteen seventies
cues.zh: 现在，请注意峰值出现在 20 世纪 70 年代

cues.en: and it's been going downhill and in the nineteen seventies it was a little over two liters a person a day and now it's down to about 1.7
cues.zh: 而且一直在走下坡路，在 20 世纪 70 年代，人均每天略多于两升，而现在已经降至大约 1.7

cues.en: liters per person each day. So we can say with confidence that any day that any one of us uses
cues.zh: 升每人每天。所以我们可以确信地说，我们当中的任何人，在任何一天只要使用了

cues.en: more than 1.7
cues.zh: 超过 1.7

cues.en: liters of petroleum directly or indirectly,
cues.zh: 升的石油（无论是直接还是间接），

cues.en: we're using more than our share.
cues.zh: 我们使用的就已经超过了我们应得的份额。

cues.en: Now, what's the average consumption in The United States? And the answer is up, it's up around eight liters a person a day. So think about the inequity that's represented there.
cues.zh: 现在，美国的人均消费量是多少？答案是上升了，大约每人每天八升。想想这背后体现出的不平等。

cues.en: Now, there's something even more important in this graph.
cues.zh: 这张图里还有更重要的东西。

cues.en: That peak in the nineteen seventies, I think that historians in the future will look back at this peak and say that was a major
cues.zh: 我认为，未来的历史学家回看二十世纪七十年代的那个峰值时，会说那是一个重大的

cues.en: turning point in all of human history.
cues.zh: 全人类历史的转折点。

cues.en: That's the point where per capita consumption
cues.zh: 那就是人均消费

cues.en: of petroleum
cues.zh: 石油

cues.en: reached its peak before it started its inevitable decline
cues.zh: 达到峰值，随后开始不可避免的下降

cues.en: and there isn't any way I can see that we can reverse that
cues.zh: 而我看不出我们有任何办法扭转那个

cues.en: trend, that downward trend,
cues.zh: 趋势，那个下降趋势，

cues.en: given the world population growth and given the fact that we are right close to the peak of world production.
cues.zh: 考虑到世界人口增长，也考虑到我们正接近世界产量的峰值。

cues.en: Well, Doctor. Hubbard addressed a committee of the Congress. He told them that the exponential phase of the industrial growth
cues.zh: 嗯，Dr. Hubbard 向国会的一个委员会作了陈述。他告诉他们，工业增长的指数阶段

cues.en: which has dominated human activities during the last couple of centuries is now drawing to a close.
cues.zh: 过去几个世纪一直主导着人类活动，如今正接近尾声。

cues.en: Yet during the last two centuries of unbroken industrial growth, we have evolved what amounts to an exponential growth culture.
cues.zh: 然而，在工业持续增长的两个世纪里，我们已经演化出一种相当于指数增长的文化。

cues.en: I would say it's more than a culture, it's our national religion
cues.zh: 我要说，这不止是一种文化，它是我们的国家宗教

cues.en: because we
cues.zh: 因为我们

cues.en: worship growth.
cues.zh: 崇拜增长。

cues.en: Pick up any newspaper, you'll see headlines such as this: State Forecast Robust Growth.
cues.zh: 随便拿起一份报纸，你都会看到这样的标题：州预测强劲增长。

cues.en: Have you ever heard of a physician diagnosing a cancer in the patient and telling the patient you have a robust cancer?
cues.zh: 你听说过医生诊断病人患了癌症，然后告诉病人你得了很“强劲”的癌症吗？

cues.en: We had Americans being killed in the Gulf War.
cues.zh: 海湾战争中有美国人丧生。

cues.en: What's this person worried about? He doesn't care about people. He doesn't care about people being killed.
cues.zh: 这个人担心什么？他不在乎人民。他不在乎人们被杀害。

cues.en: All he's worried about is, oh, the Gulf situation may hurt Colorado's growth.
cues.zh: 他唯一担心的是，海湾局势可能会影响科罗拉多州的增长。

cues.en: Now, this incredible addiction is not limited to The United States.
cues.zh: 现在，这种惊人的沉迷并不局限于美国。

cues.en: The Wall Street Journal tells us that the Japanese are so accustomed to growth that economists in Tokyo usually speak of a recession as any time the growth rate dips below
cues.zh: 《华尔街日报》告诉我们，日本人已经如此习惯于增长，以至于东京的经济学家通常把增长率低于以下水平的情况都称为衰退：

cues.en: per year.
cues.zh: 每年。

cues.en: So what do we do?
cues.zh: 那我们该怎么做？

cues.en: In the words of Winston Churchill, sometimes we have to do what is required.
cues.zh: 用温斯顿·丘吉尔的话说，有时我们必须做必须做的事。

cues.en: We must educate all of our people to
cues.zh: 我们必须让所有人都接受培训，以便

cues.en: understanding of the arithmetic and the consequences
cues.zh: 理解这些运算及其带来的后果

cues.en: of growth,
cues.zh: 增长的，

cues.en: especially in terms of populations and in terms of the earth's finite resources.
cues.zh: 尤其是在人口方面，以及地球有限资源方面。

cues.en: We must educate people to recognize the fact that growth of populations
cues.zh: 我们必须让人们认识到，人口增长

cues.en: and growth of rates of consumption of resources cannot be sustained.
cues.zh: 而资源消耗速率的增长是不可持续的。

cues.en: Now, the world is full of people who are yakking about sustainability.
cues.zh: 如今，满世界都是大谈可持续发展的人。

cues.en: Now, some of them are doing serious good things like trying to reduce energy consumption and things like this.
cues.zh: 现在，其中一些公司正在做真正有益的事情，比如努力降低能耗之类的。

cues.en: Some of them are just trying to attack the words attack the word sustainability
cues.zh: 他们中有些人只是在攻击字眼，攻击“可持续性”这个词。

cues.en: onto whatever they're doing whether it's sustainable or not. We've got to understand the first law of sustainability and it follows directly from what I've just been talking about. The first law of sustainability is this: population growth
cues.zh: 不管他们正在做的事是否可持续。我们必须理解可持续性的第一定律，它直接来自我刚才讲的内容。可持续性的第一定律是：人口增长

cues.en: and or growth in the rates of consumption of resources cannot be sustained.
cues.zh: 而且，资源消耗速率的增长是不可持续的。

cues.en: Now this follows from the arithmetic
cues.zh: 这可以从算术推导得出

cues.en: of steady growth that we've spent time developing.
cues.zh: 我们花了时间发展出的稳定增长。

cues.en: So this isn't an opinion. Opinions are debatable. This is fact.
cues.zh: 所以这不是观点。观点可以争论。这是事实。

cues.en: There's nothing here to debate. You cannot sustain population growth. You cannot sustain growth in the rates of consumption of resources.
cues.zh: 这里没有什么可争论的。你无法维持人口增长，也无法维持资源消耗率的增长。

cues.en: And so it's intellectually dishonest to talk about sustainability
cues.zh: 所以谈论可持续性在学术上是不诚实的

cues.en: without stressing the obvious fact
cues.zh: 不用强调显而易见的事实

cues.en: that stopping population growth is a necessary
cues.zh: 即停止人口增长是必要的

cues.en: condition
cues.zh: 条件

cues.en: for sustainability.
cues.zh: 为了可持续性。

cues.en: Now it's not sufficient. Stopping population growth in itself is not sufficient but there's no way you can have sustainability if you don't stop population growth.
cues.zh: 现在这还不够。仅仅停止人口增长本身是不够的，但如果不停止人口增长，就无法实现可持续性。

cues.en: We need to educate people to see the need to examine carefully the allegations of technological
cues.zh: 我们需要教育人们认识到，有必要仔细审视有关技术的各项指控。

cues.en: optimists who assure us that science and technology will always be able to solve all of our problems of population growth, food, energy and resources.
cues.zh: 乐观主义者向我们保证，科学技术总能解决人口增长、粮食、能源和资源方面的所有问题。

cues.en: Now chief among these optimists
cues.zh: 这些乐观主义者中的佼佼者

cues.en: was the late Doctor. Julian Simon,
cues.zh: 是已故的 Julian Simon 博士，

cues.en: formerly professor of economics and business administration at the University of Illinois and later at the University of Maryland.
cues.zh: 曾任伊利诺伊大学经济学与工商管理教授，后任教于马里兰大学。

cues.en: With regard to copper, Simon has written that we will never run out of copper because copper can be made from other metals.
cues.zh: 关于铜，西蒙曾写道，我们永远不会耗尽铜，因为铜可以由其他金属制成。

cues.en: Well, the letters to the editor jumped all over and told him about chemistry.
cues.zh: 结果读者来信群起而攻之，纷纷批评他，给他讲起了化学。

cues.en: He just brushed it off. He said, don't worry. If it's ever important, we'll figure out how to make copper out of other metals.
cues.zh: 他只是一笑了之。他说，别担心。如果这事真重要，我们总会想出怎么用其他金属造铜。

cues.en: Simon had a book that was published by the Princeton University Press
cues.zh: Simon有一本书，由普林斯顿大学出版社出版

cues.en: and in that book he's writing about oil from many sources including biomass and he says clearly, there's no meaning limit to this source except for the sun's energy.
cues.zh: 在书中，他写到来自多种来源的石油，包括生物质，并明确指出，除了太阳能，这种来源没有意义的上限。

cues.en: He goes on to note, but even if our sun were not so vast as it is, there may well be other suns elsewhere.
cues.zh: 他接着指出，但即使我们的太阳不像现在这样巨大，其他地方也可能有其他太阳。

cues.en: Simon's right.
cues.zh: Simon是对的。

cues.en: There are other suns elsewhere. But now the question is, would you base public policy
cues.zh: 其他地方确实有其他太阳。但现在的问题是，你会基于这样的信念来制定公共政策吗？

cues.en: on the belief that if we ever need another sun, we'll figure out how to go get it and haul it back into the solar system?
cues.zh: 即如果我们有一天需要另一个太阳，我们会想办法去获取它并把它拖回太阳系？

cues.en: Now don't laugh. For decades before his death, this man was a trusted
cues.zh: 现在别笑。在他去世前的几十年里，这个人是一位值得信赖的

cues.en: policy advisor
cues.zh: 政策顾问

cues.en: at the very highest levels in Washington DC.
cues.zh: 在华盛顿特区最高层。

cues.en: Here's a quotation from one of his strong supporters.
cues.zh: 这里引用他一位坚定支持者的话。

cues.en: There was a UN report that talked about the possibility of resource collapse because of population growth and when asked about the report, HUD Secretary Jack Kemp said nonsense,
cues.zh: 有一份联合国报告谈到了由于人口增长可能导致资源崩溃的可能性，当被问及这份报告时，住房和城市发展部部长Jack Kemp说胡说，

cues.en: People are not a drain on the resources of the planet.
cues.zh: 人不是地球资源的消耗者。

cues.en: Malcolm Forbes Junior, editor in chief of Forbes Magazine
cues.zh: Malcolm Forbes Junior，《福布斯》杂志主编

cues.en: tells us in an editorial that CNN recently ran a silly series
cues.zh: 在一篇社论中告诉我们，CNN最近播出了一个愚蠢的系列节目

cues.en: purporting to show that the world's in mortal danger because there are too many of us.
cues.zh: 声称世界正处于致命危险之中，因为我们人太多了。

cues.en: In the poorer countries, the many mouths mean poverty and richer countries are wrecking the earth's atmosphere with pollution.
cues.zh: 在较贫穷的国家，众多的人口意味着贫困，而较富裕的国家正在用污染破坏地球的大气层。

cues.en: It's all nonsense.
cues.zh: 全是胡扯。

cues.en: Bill Moyers
cues.zh: 比尔·莫耶斯

cues.en: interviewed Isaac Asimov.
cues.zh: 采访了艾萨克·阿西莫夫。

cues.en: He asked Asimov,
cues.zh: 他问阿西莫夫，

cues.en: what happens to the idea of the dignity of the human species if this population growth continues?
cues.zh: 如果人口继续这样增长下去，人类物种尊严的概念会变成什么样？

cues.en: And Asimov says it'll be completely destroyed.
cues.zh: 阿西莫夫回答说，这将彻底被毁掉。

cues.en: I like to use what I call my bathroom metaphor.
cues.zh: 我喜欢用我所谓的“卫生间隐喻”。

cues.en: If two people live in an apartment and the two bathrooms and both have freedom of the bathroom, you can go to the bathroom anytime you want, stay as long as you want for whatever you need and everyone believes in freedom of the bathroom, it should be right there in the constitution.
cues.zh: 如果两个人住在一套公寓里，有两个卫生间，并且两个人都享有使用卫生间的自由，你想什么时候去就什么时候去，想待多久就待多久，干你想干的事，每个人都坚信卫生间自由，这甚至应该写进宪法里。

cues.en: But if you have 20 people in the apartment and two bathrooms, then no matter how much every person believes in freedom of the bathroom, there's no such thing.
cues.zh: 但如果公寓里住了20个人，却只有两个卫生间，那么无论每个人多么坚信卫生间自由，这种自由都不复存在了。

cues.en: You have to set up times for each person. You have to bang on the door, aren't you through yet? And so on.
cues.zh: 你必须给每个人规定时间。你得去敲门，喊着“你还没完事吗？”诸如此类。

cues.en: And Asimov concluded with what I think is one of the most profound observations
cues.zh: 最后阿西莫夫得出了一个结论，我认为这是我多年来看到的

cues.en: I've seen in years.
cues.zh: 最深刻的洞见之一。

cues.en: Asimov says in the same way, democracy
cues.zh: 阿西莫夫说，同样地，民主

cues.en: cannot survive
cues.zh: 无法在

cues.en: overpopulation.
cues.zh: 过度人口中生存。

cues.en: Human dignity cannot survive overpopulation.
cues.zh: 人类的尊严无法在过度人口中生存。

cues.en: Convenience and decency cannot survive overpopulation.
cues.zh: 便捷与体面无法在过度人口中生存。

cues.en: As you put more and more people into the world, the value of life not only declines, it disappears. It doesn't matter if someone dies,
cues.zh: 随着世界上的人越来越多，生命的价值不仅在下降，而且消失了。某个人死了根本无所谓，

cues.en: the more people there are, the less one individual matters.
cues.zh: 人越多，单个个体就越显得无足轻重。

cues.en: Now let me give you two examples of this destruction
cues.zh: 现在让我举两个由于人口增长导致

cues.en: democracy by population growth. I joined the faculty here in 1950.
cues.zh: 民主被摧毁的例子。我在1950年加入这里的教职员工行列。

cues.en: At that time, the population of Boulder was about 20,000.
cues.zh: 当时，博尔德的人口大约是2万。

cues.en: There were nine members of the City Council. Today, it's approaching a 100,000.
cues.zh: 市议会有九名成员。如今，人口正接近10万。

cues.en: There are nine members of the City Council. So, in a little over fifty years,
cues.zh: 市议会仍有九名成员。所以，在五十多年间，

cues.en: the number of people per member of the City Council has increased by a factor of five. Democracy in Boulder has declined to 20% of what it was fifty years ago.
cues.zh: 每位市议员对应的人口数变成了原来的五倍。博尔德的民主已降到五十年前的20%。

cues.en: And the second example has to do with the year 2000 national census.
cues.zh: 第二个例子与2000年全国人口普查有关。

cues.en: This showed that in the decade of the nineties, The US population
cues.zh: 它显示，在九十年代这十年里，美国人口

cues.en: increased by about 13%.
cues.zh: 增长了约13%。

cues.en: Now this means every
cues.zh: 现在这意味着每个

cues.en: house seat in the House of Representatives
cues.zh: 众议院席位

cues.en: now has 13%
cues.zh: 现在有13%

cues.en: more constituents
cues.zh: 更多选民

cues.en: on the average
cues.zh: 平均而言

cues.en: than they did ten years ago.
cues.zh: 比十年前多。

cues.en: And in the last one hour, the world population has increased by about 10,000
cues.zh: 而在过去一小时里，世界人口增加了约1万

cues.en: people and the population of The United States in this one hour has increased by about 280
cues.zh: 人，而美国人口在这一小时里增加了约280

cues.en: people.
cues.zh: 人。

cues.en: And we have to ask,
cues.zh: 我们不得不问，

cues.en: why don't more US environmentalists
cues.zh: 为什么没有更多美国环保人士

cues.en: and environmental organizations
cues.zh: 和环保组织

cues.en: speak out about the problem of population growth here in The United States.
cues.zh: 公开谈论美国这里的人口增长问题。

cues.en: The simple arithmetic makes it absolutely clear that long term preservation of the environment
cues.zh: 简单的算术已经清楚表明，长期保护环境

cues.en: in The US is impossible in the face of continued US population growth. But you hear all sorts of political leaders say, oh, we can have our growth, we'll call it smart growth and smart growth will save the environment. Well, we need to know about smart growth. Smart growth destroys the environment.
cues.zh: 在美国，面对持续的人口增长，这是不可能的。但你会听到各种政治领袖说，哦，我们可以有增长，我们把它叫作精明增长，精明增长会拯救环境。好吧，我们需要了解精明增长。精明增长会破坏环境。

cues.en: Dumb growth destroys the environment.
cues.zh: 盲目增长会破坏环境。

cues.en: Now, growth just destroys the environment with good taste.
cues.zh: 而现在的增长，不过是包装得更体面地破坏环境罢了。

cues.en: So it's a little like buying a ticket on the Titanic. If you're smart, you go first class.
cues.zh: 这有点像买泰坦尼克号的船票。聪明人会坐头等舱，

cues.en: If you're dumb, you go steerage, but the result's the same.
cues.zh: 蠢人去坐统舱，但结局都是一样的。

cues.en: So central to the things that we must do is to recognize that population growth is the immediate cause of all of our resource and environmental
cues.zh: 因此我们必须要做的一项核心要务，就是认识到人口增长是造成我们所有资源与环境

cues.en: crises.
cues.zh: 危机的直接原因。

cues.en: And of all the crises,
cues.zh: 而在所有危机当中，

cues.en: I think this one, global warming, looms larger and more threatening than anything
cues.zh: 我认为全球变暖这个危机，比其他任何危机都更加紧迫、更具威胁。

cues.en: in all
cues.zh: 从整体的

cues.en: consumption of resources,
cues.zh: 资源消耗来看，

cues.en: we can say with confidence,
cues.zh: 我们可以确信地说，

cues.en: the world's worst population growth problem is right here in The United States. But you hear all sorts of well meaning people
cues.zh: 全球最严重的人口增长问题其实就在美国。但你总能听到各种出于好意的人，

cues.en: pointing to distant underdeveloped nations and saying they're the problem with overpopulation.
cues.zh: 指着遥远的欠发达国家说，是他们人口过剩造成了问题。

cues.en: The average person in The United States in a lifetime will consume something like maybe 30 times the amount of resources that will be consumed by a person in a lifetime in an underdeveloped nation.
cues.zh: 一个美国人一生消耗的资源，差不多是欠发达国家一个人一生消耗量的 30 倍。

cues.en: We are the problem.
cues.zh: 我们自己才是问题所在。

cues.en: We have the responsibility
cues.zh: 我们有责任，

cues.en: and we have the authority to deal with the problem here as a domestic problem in The United States.
cues.zh: 也有权力把这当作美国的国内问题来解决。

cues.en: And some years ago, speaking here on the campus of the University of Colorado,
cues.zh: 几年前，在科罗拉多大学的校园里，

cues.en: our United States Senator Tim Wirth said that the best thing we can do to help other countries stop their population growth is for us to set an example and stop our own population growth here in The US. We have sent representatives to international conferences
cues.zh: 美国参议员 Tim Wirth 就曾说过，帮助其他国家遏制人口增长最好的办法，就是我们以身作则，先遏制美国本土的人口增长。可我们却派代表参加国际会议，

cues.en: to tell the underdeveloped nations, you're the problem. You've got to stop your population growth. And they just laugh and say, look, you're the problem with all of your high per capita consumption.
cues.zh: 去对欠发达国家说：你们才是问题所在，必须控制人口增长。而他们只是笑笑说：看看你们极高的人均资源消耗量吧，你们才是问题的根源。

cues.en: Now, except for the petroleum graphs, the things I tell you are not predictions of the future. I'm only reporting facts and the results of some very simple arithmetic.
cues.zh: 除了这些石油图表之外，我告诉你们的事情都不是对未来的预测。我只是在陈述事实和一些非常简单的算术结果。

cues.en: But I do this with confidence that these facts,
cues.zh: 但我之所以有信心这样做，是因为这些事实、

cues.en: this arithmetic and more important, our level of understanding
cues.zh: 这些算术，更重要的是，我们对它们的理解水平

cues.en: of them will play a major role in shaping our future.
cues.zh: 将在塑造我们的未来中发挥重要作用。

cues.en: Now don't take what I've said blindly or uncritically because of the rhetoric or for any other reason.
cues.zh: 现在，不要因为那些言辞或任何其他原因就盲目地、不加批判地接受我所说的话。

cues.en: Please you check the facts.
cues.zh: 请你们核实事实。

cues.en: Please check my arithmetic.
cues.zh: 请核实我的算术。

cues.en: If you find errors, please let me know.
cues.zh: 如果你们发现错误，请告诉我。

cues.en: But if you don't find errors,
cues.zh: 但如果你们没有发现错误，

cues.en: then I hope you'll take this very, very seriously.
cues.zh: 那么我希望你们会非常、非常认真地对待这件事。

cues.en: You are important people.
cues.zh: 你们是重要的人。

cues.en: You can think.
cues.zh: 你们能思考。

cues.en: And if there was ever a time when the human race needs people who will think,
cues.zh: 如果说有哪个时刻人类需要会思考的人，

cues.en: it's right now. It's our responsibility
cues.zh: 那就是现在。这是我们的责任

cues.en: as citizens in a democracy
cues.zh: 作为民主社会中的公民

cues.en: to think.
cues.zh: 去思考。

cues.en: And so to be successful with this experiment of human life on earth, we have to understand
cues.zh: 所以，要让地球上人类生活这个实验成功，我们必须理解

cues.en: the laws of nature as we encounter them in the study of science and mathematics.
cues.zh: 我们在科学和数学研究中遇到的自然规律。

cues.en: We have to remember the message of this cartoon.
cues.zh: 我们必须记住这幅漫画传达的信息。

cues.en: Thinking is very upsetting.
cues.zh: 思考是一件很令人不安的事。

cues.en: It tells us things we'd rather not know.
cues.zh: 它告诉我们一些我们宁愿不知道的事情。

cues.en: We should remember the words of Galileo. He said, I do not feel obliged to believe that the same God who has endowed us with sense, reason and intellect
cues.zh: 我们应该记住伽利略的话。他说，我并不觉得必须相信，那位赋予我们感官、理性和智力的上帝

cues.en: has intended us to forego their use.
cues.zh: 有意让我们放弃使用它们。

cues.en: We should remember the words of Aldous Huxley. He observed that facts do not cease to exist because they're ignored.
cues.zh: 我们应该记住奥尔德斯·赫胥黎的话。他指出，事实并不会因为被忽视就不存在。

cues.en: And we should remember
cues.zh: 而我们应该记住

cues.en: H. L. Mencken's social philosophy.
cues.zh: H. L. Mencken 的社会哲学。

cues.en: He believed that it was of the nature of the human species to reject what is true but unpleasant
cues.zh: 他相信，人类的天性就是拒绝真实但令人不快的东西

cues.en: and to embrace what is obviously false
cues.zh: 而去拥抱明显虚假

cues.en: but comforting.
cues.zh: 却令人慰藉的东西。

cues.en: And we should remember Eric Severide's law.
cues.zh: 而我们应该记住 Eric Severide 定律。

cues.en: He was a newscaster who made the transition from radio to television back in the nineteen fifties.
cues.zh: 他是一位新闻播音员，在二十世纪五十年代从广播转向了电视。

cues.en: He observed that the chief source of problems is solutions.
cues.zh: 他观察到，问题的主要来源是解决方案。

cues.en: Now, let's just look at an example.
cues.zh: 现在，我们来看一个例子。

cues.en: The Nile River for thousands of years would flood in the spring and the silt that was carried down by the river would be deposited on agricultural lands on the two sides of the river and this renewed the fertility of the land. They had a sustainable agriculture for thousands of years.
cues.zh: 几千年来，尼罗河在春季泛滥，河水夹带的淤泥沉积在两岸的农田上，让土地重新变得肥沃。他们就这样维持了数千年的可持续农业。

cues.en: But now the flood was a sign of a nuisance as you had cities develop along there and the city people didn't like the floods and then the city people needed electricity. So that was the problem. What was the solution? The High Dam At Aswan.
cues.zh: 但如今，洪水成了一种麻烦，因为沿河发展起了城市，城里人不喜欢洪水，而且城里人需要电力。所以那就是问题。解决方案是什么？阿斯旺高坝。

cues.en: So now let's look at the problems caused by the solution. First of all, all the silt is carried down by the river, is deposited in the reservoir behind the dam. So this means the dam has a lifetime, maybe a hundred, two two hundred years. It certainly is not very long.
cues.zh: 那么现在我们来看看这个解决方案造成的问题。首先，河水夹带的所有淤泥都沉积在大坝后面的水库里。这意味着大坝是有寿命的，也许一百年、两百年。肯定不算很长。

cues.en: So it'll be filled and then there won't be the storage capacity that it was designed to have. The water that's let out from the dam today is very clear water. So this means all of the erosion patterns downstream have changed. It used to be deposit here, pick up there and so on. Now, it's pretty much just picking up because it starts out from the dam as clear water.
cues.zh: 所以它会被填满，然后就再也没有当初设计时的蓄水能力了。今天从大坝放出来的水非常清澈。这意味着下游所有的侵蚀模式都改变了。过去是这里沉积、那里冲刷，如此往复。现在基本上只有冲刷，因为水从大坝出来时就是清澈的。

cues.en: Down at the Delta in Alexandria,
cues.zh: 在亚历山大附近的三角洲，

cues.en: where the Nile enters the Mediterranean Sea,
cues.zh: 尼罗河汇入地中海的地方，

cues.en: they're washing away
cues.zh: 他们正在冲走

cues.en: agricultural land because it's no longer being deposited and the river is just washing it out into the Mediterranean.
cues.zh: 农田，因为泥沙不再沉积，河流直接把它冲进地中海。

cues.en: And it used to be the load of biological
cues.zh: 过去，这里一直有大量生物

cues.en: nutrients that were brought down in this river all the time supported a major fishery in the Eastern Mediterranean.
cues.zh: 营养物质随河水带下来，支撑了东地中海的重要渔场。

cues.en: That fishery is in serious decline because the nutrients no longer reach there. And now, in order to have their agriculture, they've got to do irrigation.
cues.zh: 那座渔场正在严重衰退，因为营养物质不再到达那里。现在，为了发展农业，他们必须灌溉。

cues.en: They've got to buy fertilizer. It takes energy to make the fertilizer and it could easily be that some of the energy to make the fertilizer comes from the dam.
cues.zh: 他们必须买肥料。制造肥料需要能源，而制造肥料的部分能源很可能来自大坝。

cues.en: And now, there are lots of more agricultural workers waiting bare foot in the irrigation ditches and they're subject to a schistomyosis,
cues.zh: 现在，更多农业工人赤脚站在灌溉沟渠里，容易患上血吸虫病，

cues.en: which is a, some kind of a parasite that's carried by things in the water that can get through the skin. If you're bare foot in the, in the water, why you get this. Everything went bad because of the solution to the problem. Nobody looked at what the problems would be caused by the solution. This is one of the most important things that we need to remember.
cues.zh: 这是一种寄生虫，由水中的生物携带，能穿透皮肤。你若赤脚在水里，就会得这个病。一切都因为问题的解决方案而变糟。没人考虑解决方案会造成什么问题。这是我们需要记住的最重要的事情之一。

cues.en: Now, here's a challenge.
cues.zh: 现在，有个挑战。

cues.en: Can you think of any problem
cues.zh: 你能想到任何问题吗

cues.en: on any scale
cues.zh: 无论什么尺度

cues.en: from microscopic to global
cues.zh: 从微观到全球

cues.en: whose long term solution
cues.zh: 其长期解决方案

cues.en: is in any demonstrable way aided, assisted or advanced by having larger populations
cues.zh: 能以任何可证明的方式，因人口更多而得到帮助、协助或推进

cues.en: at the local level, at the state level,
cues.zh: 在地方层面、在州层面，

cues.en: the national level or globally. Can you think of anything that will get better if we crowd more people into our communities, into our state, into our nation or on this earth? Think about it.
cues.zh: 国家层面或全球层面。你能想到什么会变好，如果我们把更多人挤进社区、挤进州、挤进国家，或挤到这个地球上？想一想。

cues.en: Will anything get better with increased population?
cues.zh: 人口增加会带来任何改善吗？

cues.en: And I like the words of the late Reverend Martin Luther King Junior.
cues.zh: 我很喜欢已故的马丁·路德·金牧师说过的话。

cues.en: He said, Unlike the plagues of the dark ages or contemporary diseases which we do not yet understand,
cues.zh: 他说：不同于黑暗时代的瘟疫，或那些我们至今尚未理解的当代疾病，

cues.en: the modern plague of overpopulation
cues.zh: 现代的人口过剩瘟疫

cues.en: is soluble
cues.zh: 是可以解决的

cues.en: by means we have discovered and with resources we possess.
cues.zh: 我们已经发现了解决方法，也拥有相应的资源。

cues.en: What is lacking is not sufficient knowledge of the solution
cues.zh: 我们缺少的不是对解决方案的充分了解，

cues.en: but universal consciousness of the gravity of the problem
cues.zh: 而是对问题严重性的普遍认识，

cues.en: and the education of the billions
cues.zh: 以及对数十亿人的教育，

cues.en: who are its victims.
cues.zh: 因为他们正是这个问题的受害者。

cues.en: And so I hope I've made a reasonable case for my opening statement
cues.zh: 所以，我希望自己已经为开场时的观点提供了充分的论据：

cues.en: that I believe the greatest shortcoming of the human race is our inability
cues.zh: 我认为，人类最大的缺陷，就是我们无法

cues.en: to understand this very simple
cues.zh: 理解这非常简单的

cues.en: arithmetic.
cues.zh: 算术。

cues.en: So I thank you very, very much
cues.zh: 非常非常感谢大家，

cues.en: and I would be happy to answer questions.
cues.zh: 我很乐意回答大家的问题。
